dataNote: Confirmed genuinely distinct from the existing Physics (F300) entry, not a specialization choice within it: Theoretical Physics has its own UCAS code, its own admissions page, a Year-1 Lab/Non-Lab Pathway fork not present in Physics BSc, and compulsory core modules (Foundations of Theoretical Physics, Mathematics for Quantum and Information Sciences, Advanced Dynamics and Relativistic Fields, Chaos Dynamical Systems and Complex Variables) that appear nowhere in Physics BSc's module list — in the plain Physics degree, 'Theoretical Physics' is merely one optional Year-1 elective among several. A 4-year MSci variant (F343, A*A*A/A*AAA entry, IB 7,7,6) also exists; the BSc is used as the representative entry. No Discover Uni record could be confirmed for the plain Theoretical Physics course specifically — only a differently-named, joint-sounding 'Theoretical Physics and Applied Mathematics' record was found, and it was not substituted in.

dataNote: Confirmed genuinely distinct from the existing Mathematics (G100) entry via module-by-module comparison: this course makes Data Science and Machine Learning plus Statistics compulsory core modules in Year 2 (versus Statistics being merely optional in Mathematics BSc), and requires at least half of its Year 3 optional credits to come from a defined statistics/data-science module list — a structural, compulsory curriculum divergence, not a rename. A related new-for-2026 course, Mathematical Sciences BSc (G105), was assessed and found to differ from Mathematics BSc by only one swapped Year-1 module with Years 2-3 structurally identical, and was judged too similar to warrant a separate entry. No Discover Uni data exists yet for this course — it is new for 2026/27 entry.
